page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.large is an entry-tier virtual machine instance provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with two threads on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. The instance includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results place the processing capabilities of the ecs.u0.c1m2.large in the lower percentiles across evaluated metrics. Single-core stress-ng tests record 1093.88, categorizing it in the bottom 25%, while multi-core stress-ng throughput registers at 1458.47 in the lower 10%. Memory throughput delivers 9.92 GB/sec for uncached 256MB block reads and 9.22 GB/sec for uncached writes, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 907.12. Synthetic application tests indicate 1.47 million operations per second for Redis SET workloads and 1.26 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language inference on small 135M parameter models executes at 121.75 tokens per second during prompt ingestion and 34.68 tokens per second during generation.

Given its minimal compute footprint and lower benchmark percentiles, the ecs.u0.c1m2.large offers a cost-conscious entry point for non-critical, lightweight services. The 1:2 core-to-memory balance makes it suitable for low-throughput web serving, internal development or testing environments, background utility scripts, and small batch jobs that do not require intense CPU compute, large memory tables, or bundled local disk IOPS.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.large is an entry-level compute instance built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no local storage and does not include GPU acceleration. Instruction sets include AVX-512F, AVX, and AES. Benchmark evaluations place its compute and memory bandwidth in the lower performance brackets, with a Geekbench single-core score of 919.0 and multi-core score of 1093.0, alongside 1.26 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Due to its lean resource allocation and compact memory profile, the instance functions primarily as a budget-efficient option for lightweight application hosting, background utility services, development sandboxes, and microservices that do not demand heavy concurrent processing or local disk throughput.
